answers.answer: The retention window is 30 days (RETENTION_DAYS = 30 in code, matching config/defaults.json). ADR-001 chose a fixed 30-day window over a sliding TTL because the audit trail requires a fixed boundary.

Directly, src/ingest.js imports src/store.js (and is defined by docs/DECISIONS.md). Transitively, since store imports retention, ingest depends on store -> retention. The overall chain is ingest -> store -> retention, with scheduler -> ingest separately.

The backfill path is not yet implemented and documenting it is a TODO before the next release; backfill cannot run until the store exposes a bounded writer; and there is an unresolved architecture question about whether backfill may write directly to the store or only through ingest.
A sliding TTL was rejected in favor of a fixed 30-day window, because the audit trail requires a fixed boundary (per ADR-001).
When the store lock is held, the scheduler drops the batch instead of retrying, and an alert fires if the drop counter exceeds 1 per hour.
